definitions.rationale: This macro equation defines the fresh verification syntax symbol smallestLoopBody as the exact constructor AST for one source loop iteration.
definitions.text:
rule smallestLoopBody
    => If(
         Compare(
           Subscript(Name("arr"), Name("i")),
           CmpOp(
             "!=",
             Subscript(
               Name("arr"),
               BinOp(
                 "-",
                 BinOp("-", Call(Name("len"), Name("arr")), Name("i")),
                 Int(1))))),
         AugAssign(Name("changes"), "+", Int(1)),
         .Stmts)
       AugAssign(Name("i"), "+", Int(1))

definitions.rationale: This macro equation defines the fresh verification syntax symbol smallestBody as the constructor AST for the function body.
definitions.text:
rule smallestBody
    => Assign(Name("changes"), Int(0))
       Assign(Name("i"), Int(0))
       While(
         Compare(
           Name("i"),
           CmpOp(
             "<",
             BinOp(
               "//",
               Call(Name("len"), Name("arr")),
               Int(2)))),
         smallestLoopBody)
       Return(Name("changes"))

definitions.rationale: This simplification equation defines the fresh verification summary halfLen in terms of sequence length and integer operations; it is an equation of the new symbol, not a fact about an externally defined symbol.
This equation defines the fresh mathematical summary pairDiff using the supplied comparison at mirrored sequence positions.
definitions.text:
rule pairDiff(VS:ValSeq, I:Int)
    => #if applyCmp(
              "!=",
              valSeqAt(VS, I),
              valSeqAt(VS, vsLen(VS) -Int I -Int 1))
       #then 1
       #else 0
       #fi

definitions.rationale: This is the guarded base defining equation for the fresh recursive summary mismatchCount.
definitions.text:
rule mismatchCount(_VS:ValSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int) => 0
    requires I >=Int STOP

definitions.rationale: This is the guarded recursive defining equation for the fresh summary mismatchCount, advancing the index and adding the current pair contribution.
definitions.text:
rule mismatchCount(VS:ValSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int)
    => pairDiff(VS, I) +Int mismatchCount(VS, I +Int 1, STOP)
    requires I <Int STOP

operational_rules.rationale: This rule performs an ordinary local execution step for the already-selected branch and its fixed counter AugAssign, updating the scopes cell while preserving the continuation and residual scope map. The earlier branch claims prove two separately guarded paths rather than this identical unguarded conditional rule, so it is not classified as a proved derived lemma.
operational_rules.text:
rule <k>
         #branch(
           B:Bool,
           AugAssign(Name("changes"), "+", Int(1)),
           .Stmts)
         =>
         .K
         ...
       </k>
       <env> 1 </env>
       <scopes>
         1 |-> scope(
                "arr" |-> list(VS:ValSeq)
                "changes"
                  |-> (C:Int
                       => C +Int (#if B #then 1 #else 0 #fi))
                "i" |-> I:Int,
                parent(0))
         REST:Map
       </scopes>

source_rules.rationale: This rule replaces the complete initialized loop and return configuration with the mismatch-count summary. The bridge-free loop claim proved by prove.sh is strictly more general, with arbitrary accumulator and index variables, an extra index guard, and a generalized result; it is not the identical installed statement. The installed algorithmic summary therefore remains a trusted domain lemma rather than a proved derived lemma.
source_rules.text:
rule
    <k>
      #while(
        Compare(
          Name("i"),
          CmpOp(
            "<",
            BinOp(
              "//",
              Call(Name("len"), Name("arr")),
              Int(2)))),
        smallestLoopBody)
      ~> (Return(Name("changes")) .Stmts):Stmts
      ~> #endcall
      => mismatchCount(VS, 0, halfLen(VS))
    </k>
    <env> 1 => 0 </env>
    <scopes>
      -1 |-> fixedBuiltins
      0 |-> scope(
             "smallest_change"
               |-> closureVal("arr", smallestBody, 0),
             parent(-1))
      1 |-> scope(
             "arr" |-> list(VS:ValSeq)
             "changes" |-> 0
             "i" |-> 0,
             parent(0))
      =>
      -1 |-> fixedBuiltins
      0 |-> scope(
             "smallest_change"
               |-> closureVal("arr", smallestBody, 0),
             parent(-1))
    </scopes>
    <scopeLoc> 2 => 1 </scopeLoc>
    <heap> .Map </heap>
    <heapLoc> 0 </heapLoc>
    <stack>
      ListItem(frame(.K, 0, 1))
      =>
      .List
    </stack>
    <ret> noRet </ret>
    <exc> NoExc </exc>
    <exit-code> 0 </exit-code>
    requires allInts(VS)
    [priority(40)]

source_rules.rationale: This simplification rule asserts definedness of an applyCmp expression under integer-list and index bounds. Both #Ceil and applyCmp are defined outside the verification module, so the rule is a fact about existing operations, and prove.sh contains no earlier proof of this exact statement.
source_rules.text:
rule #Ceil(
         applyCmp(
           "!=",
           valSeqAt(VS:ValSeq, I:Int),
           valSeqAt(VS, vsLen(VS) -Int I +Int -1)))
    => #Top
    requires allInts(VS)
      andBool 0 <=Int I
      andBool I <Int halfLen(VS)
    [simplification]

source_rules.rationale: This simplification rule states associativity about the pre-existing hooked integer-addition operation rather than defining a fresh verification symbol. No command in prove.sh first proves this exact equation in a module that omits it, so it is a trusted domain lemma.
